literature.Authors: Xavier Amatriain
literature.Objective: Improve recommendation accuracy beyond simple rating systems.
literature.Design/Methodology: Typically describes the algorithms or techniques used for recommendations. Look for descriptions of data processing, feature engineering, and model training.
literature.Results and Discussion: Often presents metrics like precision, recall, or NDCG to compare different recommendation strategies. Look for comparisons against baseline methods.
literature.Limitations/Assumptions: Look for discussions of data sparsity, cold-start problems, or biases in the data that might affect the recommendations.

literature.Authors: Xavier Amatriain, and Justin Basilico
literature.Objective: Enhance accuracy by incorporating user re-rating behavior.
literature.Design/Methodology: Look for sections detailing the collaborative filtering algorithms, how re-rating data is incorporated, and the experimental setup.
literature.Results and Discussion: Look for quantitative results showing improved accuracy (e.g., precision, recall, MAE, RMSE) compared to standard collaborative filtering.
literature.Limitations/Assumptions: Look for discussions of potential biases in re-rating behavior or limitations in the generalizability of the results.

literature.Design/Methodology: Look for explanations of how expert opinions are gathered, weighted, and integrated into the collaborative filtering algorithm.
literature.Results and Discussion: Look for results comparing the performance of the expert-opinion-enhanced CF to standard CF on relevant datasets.
literature.Limitations/Assumptions: Look for discussions of the challenges in identifying and validating expert opinions, or limitations in the scalability of the approach.
